interpretation: Author-written treatment guidance mapped to Invarune controls and primary-source rationale. Suggested owners and layers are proposals, not observed deployment controls. Verify applicability, enforcement, and residual exposure before accepting risk; no layer automatically lowers a finding severity or proves exploitability.

rules.plausible_impact: If external or generated content reaches this expression, it could execute Python with the process identity and access its files, credentials, and network.
rules.immediate_action: Trace the input to eval/exec and replace it with fixed operations; if generated execution is essential, isolate it before accepting untrusted input.

defense_layers.title: Enforce action policy outside the model
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Have an execution service allow only named operations, permitted argument values, and caller-owned target resources before invoking a tool.
defense_layers.verification: Exercise disallowed operations, additional arguments, cross-tenant identifiers, and direct calls that bypass the agent planner.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Authorized operations can still be harmful when business constraints are incomplete; prompt instructions cannot enforce this boundary.

defense_layers.title: Isolate tool execution
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Run the risky tool in a separate, disposable identity with no host mounts, ambient credentials, or unnecessary outbound access.
defense_layers.verification: In a test environment, attempt reads outside the workspace, forbidden network connections, and resource exhaustion; retain policy and denial evidence.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Isolation limits reachable assets; it does not make injected code trustworthy or rule out a runtime escape.

rules.plausible_impact: If a caller or agent controls command content, shell syntax could alter the intended operation and execute with the tool process permissions.
rules.immediate_action: Remove shell interpretation, select a fixed executable, and validate each argument and permitted option.

rules.immediate_action: Replace os.system/os.popen with a fixed executable and validated argument list; trace all contributing values.

rules.plausible_impact: If an unsafe loader processes attacker-controlled YAML, it may construct executable objects with application privileges.
rules.immediate_action: Use a safe YAML loader, verify that custom constructors do not restore unsafe behavior, and validate the resulting data.

defense_layers.title: Validate structure and impose parsing limits
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Accept a small explicit data schema and bound input bytes, nesting, collection sizes, and processing time before downstream use.
defense_layers.verification: Reject unexpected types and fields and oversized or deeply nested inputs; verify termination and resource limits under load.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A valid schema cannot make an executable deserializer safe or establish that the content is authorized.

rules.plausible_impact: If an attacker can supply or replace the serialized input, loading it may execute code even before the application examines the returned object.
rules.immediate_action: Establish who can produce and replace the input; migrate to a nonexecutable data format or restrict verified legacy artifacts to an isolated conversion path.

defense_layers.title: Verify artifact identity before use
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Require reviewed artifact provenance plus a digest or signature checked against an independently trusted identity or manifest.
defense_layers.verification: Substitute bytes, producer identity, or verification metadata in a controlled test and confirm the consumer rejects the artifact.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Authenticity establishes the producer and bytes; an approved producer can still ship vulnerable or malicious content.

defense_layers.title: Separate artifact conversion from production
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Perform necessary conversion of legacy serialized artifacts in a disposable environment without production data or credentials.
defense_layers.verification: Demonstrate that a conversion job cannot reach production services and only approved output formats are promoted.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Conversion output still needs integrity, format, and downstream behavior review; isolation is not proof of benign content.

rules.plausible_impact: If a network intermediary can impersonate the destination, disabled verification may expose or alter credentials, prompts, and tool responses.
rules.immediate_action: Enable certificate and hostname verification; install the intended CA for a private gateway and test rejection of an untrusted certificate.

defense_layers.title: Require authenticated encrypted transport
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Use verified TLS on every relevant network hop, with an appropriate public or private CA and validated service hostname.
defense_layers.verification: Present an untrusted, expired, or wrong-host certificate and verify rejection; inspect backend traffic after TLS termination.
defense_layers.residual_limit: TLS does not protect data from an authorized endpoint, compromised gateway, or plaintext segments beyond termination.

defense_layers.title: Restrict outbound destinations independently
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Enforce an outbound policy outside the application that permits only required destinations and services; include IPv6 and proxy paths.
defense_layers.verification: From the deployed identity, test direct IP, DNS, redirect, metadata-service, and proxy-mediated attempts to prohibited destinations.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Allowed destinations may themselves accept leaked data; destination rules do not replace content and action authorization.

rules.plausible_impact: If a browser can reach this service, permissive origin handling may allow an unintended site to interact with or read responses; actual impact depends on authentication and browser behavior.
rules.immediate_action: Identify intended browser clients, restrict allowed origins, and verify MCP Origin checks on each reachable HTTP endpoint.

defense_layers.title: Validate browser origin at the MCP listener
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Reject disallowed Origin values at the HTTP MCP endpoint and keep the allowed list limited to intended browser clients.
defense_layers.verification: Send requests with permitted and unapproved origins through each ingress path, including the direct backend path.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Origin checks and CORS behavior do not authenticate non-browser clients; missing-Origin handling needs its own policy.

defense_layers.title: Authenticate and authorize protected requests
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Authenticate each protected request and enforce tool, tenant, and target permissions at the service handling the operation.
defense_layers.verification: Test missing, expired, wrong-audience, and revoked credentials, plus a valid caller requesting a forbidden target.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Authentication identifies a caller; it does not make their supplied data safe or grant every authenticated caller equal authority.

rules.plausible_impact: If ingress rules expose the wildcard listener to unintended clients, agent or MCP operations may become reachable beyond the expected local trust boundary.
rules.immediate_action: Confirm actual listener reachability; bind local-only services to loopback or document and test the controls for intentional remote access.

defense_layers.title: Restrict network ingress
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Expose the listener only to required clients through explicit bind addresses and network access rules; close unused ports.
defense_layers.verification: Probe from allowed and forbidden network segments, including direct backend addresses and alternate address families.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Network location does not establish caller identity or protect against a compromised permitted client.

rules.plausible_impact: If debug behavior is active on a reachable deployment, errors or a framework debugger may disclose internals or permit additional actions.
rules.immediate_action: Verify the effective deployed setting, disable debug behavior, and confirm representative errors do not expose a debugger or sensitive details.

defense_layers.title: Separate operational diagnostics from client errors
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Return minimal errors to clients and retain necessary diagnostic detail only in protected, redacted server-side records.
defense_layers.verification: Trigger representative failures and confirm public responses exclude stack traces, credentials, paths, and debug consoles.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Redaction can miss unexpected formats, and authorized log readers may still see sensitive operational context.

defense_layers.title: Enforce reviewed deployment defaults
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Gate releases on approved runtime settings and reject deployments that restore the unsafe option through overrides.
defense_layers.verification: Evaluate the rendered deployment and running workload, then attempt a rollout containing the forbidden override.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A source configuration or successful build does not establish the effective production runtime policy.

rules.plausible_impact: If the detected literal is a live credential, anyone with access to the source, image layers, or copied artifacts may use its granted permissions.
rules.immediate_action: Determine whether the value is real without reproducing it; revoke or rotate a real exposed credential and remove retained copies through the incident process.

defense_layers.title: Investigate and contain confirmed secret exposure
defense_layers.how_it_helps: For a real exposed credential, identify reachable systems, revoke or rotate it, and review access records for misuse.
defense_layers.verification: Confirm the old credential no longer works and record the exposure window, affected copies, and follow-up owner.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Successful rotation stops future use of that credential but cannot reverse access or data loss that already occurred.

defense_layers.title: Use managed credential injection and revocation
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Load secrets at runtime through an approved store or workload identity; keep them out of source, artifacts, and model context.
defense_layers.verification: Test rotation and revocation without disclosing values; inspect build layers and launch metadata for retained copies.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Deleting a file or hiding a later image layer does not revoke a credential or erase copies already distributed.

defense_layers.title: Limit credentials available to the workload
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Give this component a distinct identity and only the downstream scopes and lifetime needed for its approved operations.
defense_layers.verification: Use its runtime identity to attempt forbidden service operations, then revoke it and confirm subsequent access fails.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A compromised component can still use its allowed permissions until credentials expire or revocation takes effect.

rules.plausible_impact: If path checks can be bypassed, an external value may select files outside the intended workspace, including data or executable configuration.
rules.immediate_action: Validate the final path against the intended root and review symlink and concurrent-change handling for the actual file operation.

defense_layers.title: Enforce a real filesystem boundary
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Run the tool with access only to its intended workspace and temporary area; remove sensitive mounts and inherited write access.
defense_layers.verification: Attempt traversal, absolute paths, symlink escapes, and writes outside the workspace using the actual runtime identity.
defense_layers.residual_limit: MCP roots are a cooperation signal rather than a sandbox; permissions and mount policy must enforce containment.

defense_layers.title: Make file authorization resistant to races
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Authorize the final target and use safe atomic file operations that do not follow attacker-controlled links unexpectedly.
defense_layers.verification: Test concurrent link replacement, traversal variants, pre-existing destination files, and create-versus-overwrite semantics.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A path check followed by an unrelated open can race; filesystem and operating-system differences require runtime verification.

rules.plausible_impact: If another local actor can create the predicted temporary path first, the operation may overwrite or disclose unintended files.
rules.immediate_action: Replace name-only temporary allocation with atomic creation and preserve restrictive permissions for the full operation.

defense_layers.title: Give temporary work a private lifetime
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Allocate a private temporary directory atomically, use restrictive permissions, and remove it after success or failure.
defense_layers.verification: Confirm another local identity cannot pre-create or read its files and that interrupted jobs leave no sensitive artifacts.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Permissions do not isolate processes sharing the same identity; crashes and retained backups can leave copies.

defense_layers.title: Enforce a real filesystem boundary

defense_layers.residual_limit: MCP roots are a cooperation signal rather than a sandbox; permissions and mount policy must enforce containment.

rules.plausible_impact: If unverified claims authorize a request, a caller may forge identity or privileges without possessing a valid issuer-signed token.
rules.immediate_action: Verify signatures and an explicit algorithm allowlist, trusted issuer, intended audience, expiry, and required claims before authorization.

defense_layers.title: Authorize downstream effects separately
defense_layers.how_it_helps: For each effect, check caller identity, tenant, operation, and target at the executing service using bounded downstream credentials.
defense_layers.verification: Try read-only users against writes, other-tenant identifiers, and direct tool calls without an agent session.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Correct token verification alone cannot prevent an authorized but overly broad or harmful business operation.

rules.immediate_action: Resolve and approve exact executable and transitive artifacts, enforce the lock at launch, and minimize inherited environment secrets.

defense_layers.verification: Build in a clean environment and compare resolved bytes; modify a lock or artifact and verify the release gate rejects it.
defense_layers.residual_limit: An exact version or digest can still identify a vulnerable artifact; mutable transitive dependencies must also be constrained.

rules.plausible_impact: If a referenced tag or branch moves, a workflow may execute changed third-party code with the job token, secrets, and runner access.
rules.immediate_action: Pin the action to a reviewed full commit SHA from its intended repository and review updates through the normal change process.

defense_layers.title: Limit authority in build jobs
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Give each job only required token permissions and secrets; separate untrusted contribution jobs from privileged release jobs.
defense_layers.verification: Test a contribution workflow and confirm it cannot access release credentials, protected environments, or writable repository permissions.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A pinned action still runs code with its assigned authority; compromised trusted jobs can misuse that authority.

defense_layers.title: Keep pinned artifacts maintained
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Review known-vulnerability and maintenance evidence for the actual resolved artifacts and apply updates through a repeatable release process.
defense_layers.verification: Demonstrate a dependency update, relevant regression checks, and deployment or rollback of the resulting approved artifact.
defense_layers.residual_limit: This source/image scan does not provide a current CVE verdict, and a vulnerability database cannot identify every unknown flaw.

rules.plausible_impact: If this is the effective runtime user, a tool compromise may gain more authority within the container; host impact depends on mounts, capabilities, user mappings, and kernel isolation.
rules.immediate_action: Verify the final build stage and deployed user, then run with a dedicated nonroot identity unless a documented operation requires otherwise.

defense_layers.title: Apply runtime isolation controls together
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Use a dedicated nonroot identity, minimal capabilities, no privilege escalation, and an enforced syscall and mandatory-access policy where supported.
defense_layers.verification: Inspect the effective workload and attempt privileged operations, prohibited syscalls, and access to protected host resources.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Nonroot alone is insufficient; writable mounts, added capabilities, host namespaces, and kernel flaws can weaken isolation.

defense_layers.title: Separate risky tools from sensitive workloads
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Place tools needing exceptional privileges in a separate environment with narrow interfaces and no unrelated tenant data.
defense_layers.verification: Test cross-workload network and filesystem access and confirm the privileged component cannot impersonate the requesting agent.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Shared kernels or administrative infrastructure may retain common failure paths; a container is not automatically a strong hostile-code boundary.

rules.plausible_impact: If the privileged or escalation setting is effective, a compromised tool may access host capabilities or resources that ordinary container isolation would restrict.

defense_layers.residual_limit: Correct token verification alone cannot prevent an authorized but overly broad or harmful business operation.

defense_layers.title: Bind sensitive actions to explicit approval
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Require an independent approval for the exact actor, tool, normalized arguments, target, and expiry before irreversible effects occur.
defense_layers.verification: Change arguments after approval, replay the approval, and call after expiry; each attempt must be denied before a side effect.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Approval cannot compensate for misleading previews, excessive approver authority, or actions that happen before the check.

defense_layers.title: Limit credentials available to the workload
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Give this component a distinct identity and only the downstream scopes and lifetime needed for its approved operations.
defense_layers.verification: Use its runtime identity to attempt forbidden service operations, then revoke it and confirm subsequent access fails.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A compromised component can still use its allowed permissions until credentials expire or revocation takes effect.

rules.plausible_impact: If arbitrary inbound tokens are forwarded to another resource, audience boundaries and the downstream service consent model may be bypassed.
rules.immediate_action: Disable passthrough, validate the MCP resource audience, and acquire separately authorized downstream credentials for the intended operation.

defense_layers.title: Use resource-specific downstream credentials
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Obtain downstream credentials for the intended service and caller-authorized scopes, rather than forwarding the inbound MCP token.
defense_layers.verification: Send tokens with another audience and attempt delegation beyond the caller scope; confirm both are denied.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A valid downstream token can still be overprivileged; consent, token storage, and each operation need separate review.

defense_layers.title: Authorize downstream effects separately
defense_layers.how_it_helps: For each effect, check caller identity, tenant, operation, and target at the executing service using bounded downstream credentials.
defense_layers.verification: Try read-only users against writes, other-tenant identifiers, and direct tool calls without an agent session.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Correct token verification alone cannot prevent an authorized but overly broad or harmful business operation.

rules.plausible_impact: If remote traffic traverses an unprotected link, observers or intermediaries may read or modify MCP credentials, requests, and responses.
rules.immediate_action: Use HTTPS with verified certificates; if a separate protected transport is intentional, document and test every network hop and termination boundary.

defense_layers.title: Require authenticated encrypted transport
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Use verified TLS on every relevant network hop, with an appropriate public or private CA and validated service hostname.
defense_layers.verification: Present an untrusted, expired, or wrong-host certificate and verify rejection; inspect backend traffic after TLS termination.
defense_layers.residual_limit: TLS does not protect data from an authorized endpoint, compromised gateway, or plaintext segments beyond termination.

defense_layers.title: Limit credentials available to the workload
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Give this component a distinct identity and only the downstream scopes and lifetime needed for its approved operations.
defense_layers.verification: Use its runtime identity to attempt forbidden service operations, then revoke it and confirm subsequent access fails.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A compromised component can still use its allowed permissions until credentials expire or revocation takes effect.

rules.plausible_impact: If a durable privileged key is bundled or sent to a browser, users or injected scripts can obtain and use it outside the intended interface.
rules.immediate_action: Inspect the built client and runtime requests; move durable credentials to a trusted backend or use a provider-designed, scoped short-lived client token.

defense_layers.title: Keep privileged service access behind a backend
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Have a trusted backend hold durable provider credentials and authorize each client operation, including model, tool, spend, and data scope.
defense_layers.verification: Inspect built browser assets and network traffic for durable secrets; attempt calls beyond the current user permission and quota.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A backend can become a confused deputy if authorization is missing; a browser-designed short-lived token still needs narrow scope.

defense_layers.title: Use managed credential injection and revocation
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Load secrets at runtime through an approved store or workload identity; keep them out of source, artifacts, and model context.
defense_layers.verification: Test rotation and revocation without disclosing values; inspect build layers and launch metadata for retained copies.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Deleting a file or hiding a later image layer does not revoke a credential or erase copies already distributed.

rules.plausible_impact: If unrestricted execution or disabled approval is effective, malicious context or an erroneous plan may reach sensitive actions with the agent identity.
rules.immediate_action: Review the effective permission policy and restore bounded tools and runtime isolation; require independent approval for the specific sensitive effects.

defense_layers.title: Enforce action policy outside the model
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Have an execution service allow only named operations, permitted argument values, and caller-owned target resources before invoking a tool.
defense_layers.verification: Exercise disallowed operations, additional arguments, cross-tenant identifiers, and direct calls that bypass the agent planner.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Authorized operations can still be harmful when business constraints are incomplete; prompt instructions cannot enforce this boundary.

defense_layers.title: Bind sensitive actions to explicit approval
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Require an independent approval for the exact actor, tool, normalized arguments, target, and expiry before irreversible effects occur.
defense_layers.verification: Change arguments after approval, replay the approval, and call after expiry; each attempt must be denied before a side effect.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Approval cannot compensate for misleading previews, excessive approver authority, or actions that happen before the check.

defense_layers.title: Isolate tool execution
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Run the risky tool in a separate, disposable identity with no host mounts, ambient credentials, or unnecessary outbound access.
defense_layers.verification: In a test environment, attempt reads outside the workspace, forbidden network connections, and resource exhaustion; retain policy and denial evidence.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Isolation limits reachable assets; it does not make injected code trustworthy or rule out a runtime escape.

rules.plausible_impact: If external content is promoted into privileged instructions, an attacker may redirect the agent toward unauthorized data access or tool use.
rules.immediate_action: Keep external values outside trusted instruction templates and trace their provenance; enforce any security decision outside the model.

defense_layers.title: Keep external content outside privileged instructions
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Maintain trusted instruction templates and explicit provenance for retrieved content, tool results, and memory used as data.
defense_layers.verification: Trace each context source and test malicious instructions embedded in retrieval, tool metadata, and multi-step tool results.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Labels, delimiters, filters, and model judgments are fallible; they cannot substitute for enforced action and data-access policy.

defense_layers.title: Enforce action policy outside the model
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Have an execution service allow only named operations, permitted argument values, and caller-owned target resources before invoking a tool.
defense_layers.verification: Exercise disallowed operations, additional arguments, cross-tenant identifiers, and direct calls that bypass the agent planner.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Authorized operations can still be harmful when business constraints are incomplete; prompt instructions cannot enforce this boundary.

defense_layers.title: Exercise the complete configured agent
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Run representative injection and tool-abuse scenarios with realistic permissions, multi-step workflows, and useful-task success criteria.
defense_layers.verification: Record denied and successful actions, repeat stochastic cases, and retain counterexamples when a model or integration changes.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A passing sample or benchmark does not establish universal resistance; results apply to the tested configuration and attack set.

rules.plausible_impact: If this value is a real secret, log readers, exporters, or retained telemetry copies may gain its permissions beyond the original application boundary.
rules.immediate_action: Verify the logged value safely, remove it before formatting/export, and rotate it if real exposure is confirmed.

defense_layers.title: Minimize and protect retained telemetry
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Collect only necessary nonsecret events, redact before export, and limit access, retention, and downstream replication.
defense_layers.verification: Inject recognizable synthetic secret values and trace their absence through application, proxy, tracing, and archived logs.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Redaction tests cover selected formats; already exported copies and authorized readers remain part of the exposure assessment.

defense_layers.title: Limit credentials available to the workload
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Give this component a distinct identity and only the downstream scopes and lifetime needed for its approved operations.
defense_layers.verification: Use its runtime identity to attempt forbidden service operations, then revoke it and confirm subsequent access fails.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A compromised component can still use its allowed permissions until credentials expire or revocation takes effect.

rules.plausible_impact: If the query value is a real credential, browser history, proxies, access logs, traces, or copied links may retain a reusable secret.
rules.immediate_action: Remove the credential from the URL, use the supported authorization mechanism, and rotate real credentials while investigating retained copies.

defense_layers.title: Minimize and protect retained telemetry
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Collect only necessary nonsecret events, redact before export, and limit access, retention, and downstream replication.
defense_layers.verification: Inject recognizable synthetic secret values and trace their absence through application, proxy, tracing, and archived logs.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Redaction tests cover selected formats; already exported copies and authorized readers remain part of the exposure assessment.

defense_layers.title: Investigate and contain confirmed secret exposure
defense_layers.how_it_helps: For a real exposed credential, identify reachable systems, revoke or rotate it, and review access records for misuse.
defense_layers.verification: Confirm the old credential no longer works and record the exposure window, affected copies, and follow-up owner.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Successful rotation stops future use of that credential but cannot reverse access or data loss that already occurred.

rules.plausible_impact: If an untrusted model checkpoint reaches unsafe loading, object deserialization may execute code with the model worker permissions.
rules.immediate_action: Use a nonexecutable tensor format or a maintained, appropriate restricted loader; verify provenance, patch affected runtimes, and isolate necessary legacy conversion.

defense_layers.title: Verify artifact identity before use
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Require reviewed artifact provenance plus a digest or signature checked against an independently trusted identity or manifest.
defense_layers.verification: Substitute bytes, producer identity, or verification metadata in a controlled test and confirm the consumer rejects the artifact.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Authenticity establishes the producer and bytes; an approved producer can still ship vulnerable or malicious content.

defense_layers.title: Separate artifact conversion from production
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Perform necessary conversion of legacy serialized artifacts in a disposable environment without production data or credentials.
defense_layers.verification: Demonstrate that a conversion job cannot reach production services and only approved output formats are promoted.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Conversion output still needs integrity, format, and downstream behavior review; isolation is not proof of benign content.

defense_layers.title: Keep pinned artifacts maintained
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Review known-vulnerability and maintenance evidence for the actual resolved artifacts and apply updates through a repeatable release process.
defense_layers.verification: Demonstrate a dependency update, relevant regression checks, and deployment or rollback of the resulting approved artifact.
defense_layers.residual_limit: This source/image scan does not provide a current CVE verdict, and a vulnerability database cannot identify every unknown flaw.

rules.plausible_impact: If untrusted values are inserted as SQL syntax, they may alter a query to read or change unintended records within the database identity authority.
rules.immediate_action: Bind values as parameters and allowlist any dynamic identifiers or operation choices; trace generated and tool-supplied query fragments.

defense_layers.title: Constrain the database identity and operation set
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Use dedicated database credentials with only the required tables, rows, and operations; separate administrative access from agent tools.
defense_layers.verification: Using the agent identity, attempt schema changes, other-tenant records, unrestricted exports, and unauthorized writes.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Database permissions bound damage but cannot make a permitted query correct; query parameters do not safely bind identifiers.

defense_layers.title: Authorize downstream effects separately
defense_layers.how_it_helps: For each effect, check caller identity, tenant, operation, and target at the executing service using bounded downstream credentials.
defense_layers.verification: Try read-only users against writes, other-tenant identifiers, and direct tool calls without an agent session.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Correct token verification alone cannot prevent an authorized but overly broad or harmful business operation.

rules.plausible_impact: If an untrusted archive is extracted without effective restrictions, members may escape the target directory, overwrite data, or exhaust resources.
rules.immediate_action: Check the deployed Python behavior and explicitly use a supported safe filter plus member validation; extract into a new isolated directory.

defense_layers.title: Bound archive processing and isolate its output
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Validate member types and limits, reject unnecessary links, and enforce disk, memory, CPU, file-count, and expanded-byte budgets.
defense_layers.verification: Test traversal, links, repeated names, oversized members, archive bombs, and interruption cleanup in a disposable directory.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A safe extraction filter does not stop resource exhaustion or protect a destination concurrently modified by another process.

defense_layers.title: Enforce a real filesystem boundary
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Run the tool with access only to its intended workspace and temporary area; remove sensitive mounts and inherited write access.
defense_layers.verification: Attempt traversal, absolute paths, symlink escapes, and writes outside the workspace using the actual runtime identity.
defense_layers.residual_limit: MCP roots are a cooperation signal rather than a sandbox; permissions and mount policy must enforce containment.

rules.plausible_impact: If this value protects authentication, authorization, or replay prevention, a predictable generator may allow guessing or reuse; a nonsecurity correlation value may be harmless.
rules.immediate_action: Confirm the value purpose and replace security-sensitive generation with a cryptographically secure API and sufficient entropy.

defense_layers.title: Bound token use, scope, and replay
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Bind security tokens or state handles to their intended identity and purpose, expire them promptly, and reject inappropriate reuse.
defense_layers.verification: Try another user, another operation, repeated redemption, and use after expiry against the real verification endpoint.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Expiry and rate limits cannot replace unpredictable token generation; some protocols legitimately permit reuse within a bounded session.

defense_layers.title: Authenticate and authorize protected requests
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Authenticate each protected request and enforce tool, tenant, and target permissions at the service handling the operation.
defense_layers.verification: Test missing, expired, wrong-audience, and revoked credentials, plus a valid caller requesting a forbidden target.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Authentication identifies a caller; it does not make their supplied data safe or grant every authenticated caller equal authority.

rules.plausible_impact: If a user or agent controls template source, server-side expressions may access objects or execute behavior with the renderer privileges.
rules.immediate_action: Use a trusted fixed template and pass external values only as data; isolate any deliberate untrusted template authoring.

defense_layers.title: Keep template evaluation away from secrets and authority
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Use fixed templates and a minimal data model; isolate any intentional untrusted template authoring from application services and credentials.
defense_layers.verification: Try template expressions that access objects, files, process state, or expensive computation in a controlled test.
defense_layers.residual_limit: HTML escaping does not prevent server-side template execution; a template sandbox needs its own maintenance and bypass testing.

defense_layers.title: Isolate tool execution
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Run the risky tool in a separate, disposable identity with no host mounts, ambient credentials, or unnecessary outbound access.
defense_layers.verification: In a test environment, attempt reads outside the workspace, forbidden network connections, and resource exhaustion; retain policy and denial evidence.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Isolation limits reachable assets; it does not make injected code trustworthy or rule out a runtime escape.

rules.plausible_impact: If unsanitized agent or tool content reaches a raw HTML sink, attacker-controlled markup may execute in a viewer browser and access that viewer session.
rules.immediate_action: Render external output as text or apply a maintained, context-appropriate sanitizer before the sink; verify the final rendering path.

defense_layers.title: Apply browser defenses around rendered output
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Render data as text by default; where HTML is essential, use a maintained sanitizer and a restrictive Content Security Policy.
defense_layers.verification: Exercise active markup, event handlers, URL schemes, and sanitizer bypass regressions in the actual rendering component.
defense_layers.residual_limit: CSP is an additional layer and can be weakened by unsafe directives; sanitization must match the eventual HTML or URL context.

defense_layers.title: Isolate untrusted previews from privileged sessions
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Place intentionally active external previews on a separate origin or an appropriately restricted sandbox, without application credentials or privileged messaging capabilities.
defense_layers.verification: Attempt parent-frame access, navigation, storage access, and privileged postMessage calls from the preview; confirm explicit rejection.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Sandbox permissions can restore dangerous authority, and origin isolation does not make downloaded content safe to execute elsewhere.

rules.plausible_impact: If the unauthenticated inspector is reachable, another client may access connected MCP servers with the inspector process permissions.
rules.immediate_action: Re-enable inspector authorization and restrict its listeners and origins to the intended development environment.

defense_layers.title: Restrict network ingress
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Expose the listener only to required clients through explicit bind addresses and network access rules; close unused ports.
defense_layers.verification: Probe from allowed and forbidden network segments, including direct backend addresses and alternate address families.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Network location does not establish caller identity or protect against a compromised permitted client.

defense_layers.title: Validate browser origin at the MCP listener
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Reject disallowed Origin values at the HTTP MCP endpoint and keep the allowed list limited to intended browser clients.
defense_layers.verification: Send requests with permitted and unapproved origins through each ingress path, including the direct backend path.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Origin checks and CORS behavior do not authenticate non-browser clients; missing-Origin handling needs its own policy.

defense_layers.title: Limit credentials available to the workload
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Give this component a distinct identity and only the downstream scopes and lifetime needed for its approved operations.
defense_layers.verification: Use its runtime identity to attempt forbidden service operations, then revoke it and confirm subsequent access fails.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A compromised component can still use its allowed permissions until credentials expire or revocation takes effect.

rules.plausible_impact: If host namespaces are effective, the workload may observe host processes or bypass expected network separation, depending on its remaining privileges and deployment.
rules.immediate_action: Remove host PID/network namespace use where possible; narrowly scope and isolate any documented operational exception.

defense_layers.title: Apply runtime isolation controls together
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Use a dedicated nonroot identity, minimal capabilities, no privilege escalation, and an enforced syscall and mandatory-access policy where supported.
defense_layers.verification: Inspect the effective workload and attempt privileged operations, prohibited syscalls, and access to protected host resources.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Nonroot alone is insufficient; writable mounts, added capabilities, host namespaces, and kernel flaws can weaken isolation.

defense_layers.title: Separate risky tools from sensitive workloads
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Place tools needing exceptional privileges in a separate environment with narrow interfaces and no unrelated tenant data.
defense_layers.verification: Test cross-workload network and filesystem access and confirm the privileged component cannot impersonate the requesting agent.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Shared kernels or administrative infrastructure may retain common failure paths; a container is not automatically a strong hostile-code boundary.

rules.plausible_impact: A tool description or skill instruction can be inserted into model context before invocation; an override directive attempts to cross the boundary from external data into agent authority.
rules.immediate_action: Quarantine the affected tool/skill revision until its override text has been reviewed; remove unrelated directives and reapprove the exact content hash.

defense_layers.title: Enforce effect and data policy outside model text
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Replace the instruction with a factual description of inputs, outputs and side effects. Treat returned/retrieved text as data and enforce allowed operations in code outside the model.
defense_layers.verification: Replay the exact instruction in an isolated agent with harmless canary data and assert the policy-restricted action is denied.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A removed literal phrase does not establish immunity to indirect, multilingual, encoded or dynamically generated prompt injection.

defense_layers.title: Review and bind the exact tool/skill revision
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Pin or hash approved artifacts, review changed instructions and metadata, and require deliberate reapproval before use.
defense_layers.verification: Modify a harmless tool description or skill instruction and verify the client rejects the stale approval.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Artifact integrity preserves the approved bytes; it does not prove those bytes are safe or that remote dependencies stay unchanged.

rules.plausible_impact: An instruction that directs an agent to gather a credential or sensitive file and send it to a URL/email can turn an otherwise legitimate tool into a disclosure path.
rules.immediate_action: Inspect the named data and destination with the owner. Remove unapproved transfer instructions; rotate real credentials only if exposure is established or credibly suspected.

defense_layers.title: Enforce effect and data policy outside model text
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Use a broker that supplies audience-bound short-lived credentials without placing raw secrets in model context. Allowlist outbound recipients and show the exact payload/recipient for required approval.
defense_layers.verification: Use fake canary credentials and an isolated sink; verify an unapproved destination and encoded/piecemeal disclosure are blocked without transmitting real secrets.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Static text cannot establish destination ownership, user consent, live egress enforcement or whether the sensitive object exists.

defense_layers.title: Review and bind the exact tool/skill revision
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Pin or hash approved artifacts, review changed instructions and metadata, and require deliberate reapproval before use.
defense_layers.verification: Modify a harmless tool description or skill instruction and verify the client rejects the stale approval.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Artifact integrity preserves the approved bytes; it does not prove those bytes are safe or that remote dependencies stay unchanged.

rules.plausible_impact: Concealment or approval-bypass text in skills/tool descriptions can induce the planner to exceed user-authorized actions under the agent or MCP process identity.
rules.immediate_action: Remove the concealment/bypass directive and suspend autonomous use of the affected revision pending review.

defense_layers.title: Enforce effect and data policy outside model text
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Have the execution service validate authorization and exact arguments before action; log the operation and reject replayed or changed approvals independently of prompt instructions.
defense_layers.verification: Exercise the offending instruction with harmless actions, changed arguments, direct MCP calls and a missing/expired approval; all unauthorized effects must fail.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A visible approval prompt alone does not prove the executed target and arguments match what the user approved.

defense_layers.title: Review and bind the exact tool/skill revision
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Pin or hash approved artifacts, review changed instructions and metadata, and require deliberate reapproval before use.
defense_layers.verification: Modify a harmless tool description or skill instruction and verify the client rejects the stale approval.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Artifact integrity preserves the approved bytes; it does not prove those bytes are safe or that remote dependencies stay unchanged.

rules.plausible_impact: A client may prioritize tools or reduce consent using annotations; a destructive description or resolved direct Python write paired with readOnlyHint=true exposes a conflicting tool contract. Actual execution and authorization remain unverified.
rules.immediate_action: Temporarily handle the tool as potentially mutating; inspect its implementation and effective permissions before enabling autonomous calls.

defense_layers.title: Enforce effect and data policy outside model text
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Correct readOnlyHint and the description together, version or hash the metadata, and reapprove changed definitions. Enforce read-only credentials or server-side mutation checks independently of the annotation.
defense_layers.verification: Run against a disposable fixture and compare its before/after state; verify direct unauthorized writes fail even when the client trusts readOnlyHint.
defense_layers.residual_limit: A consistent description and annotation can still be dishonest; this check does not prove actual read-only behavior or detect all tool substitution.

defense_layers.title: Review and bind the exact tool/skill revision
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Pin or hash approved artifacts, review changed instructions and metadata, and require deliberate reapproval before use.
defense_layers.verification: Modify a harmless tool description or skill instruction and verify the client rejects the stale approval.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Artifact integrity preserves the approved bytes; it does not prove those bytes are safe or that remote dependencies stay unchanged.

rules.plausible_impact: A local actor or adjacent agent can modify shared instructions, executable artifacts or data before a more privileged worker consumes them.
rules.immediate_action: Restrict the affected path to its intended owner or group, verify ownership, and review existing writable artifacts before reuse.

defense_layers.title: Separate writable workspaces from trusted artifacts
defense_layers.how_it_helps: Isolate each tenant or worker filesystem; mount trusted skills, tool code and credentials without write permission for untrusted identities.
defense_layers.verification: Use two unrelated runtime identities and attempt to replace a harmless script or neighboring workspace file; retain the denied operation evidence.
defense_layers.residual_limit: Permissions and isolation must be validated in the actual deployment, including mounts, ownership and ACLs.
